newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Ex-Sandinista denies involvement in MRTA attack.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Sandinista denies involvement in MRTA attack.

text.p: A former Sandinista official mentioned as a leader of leftist rebels holding hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru has denied involvement in the siege, a Nicaraguan newspaper reported on Saturday.

Rodolfo Klein Samanez, identified by Peruvian intelligence as one of three leaders of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels who carried out the attack on Tuesday, worked for various years in the left-wing Sandinista government's Interior Ministry during the 1980s.
The Interior Ministry, which has since been disbanded, was the Sandinista agency in charge of internal security.
The newspaper El Nuevo Diario, Nicaragua's largest circulation daily, reported receiving a faxed letter from Klein sent from Europe denying his involvement in the attack.
"I have nothing, absolutely nothing to do with what is going on (in Peru). For the past five years I have worked with humanitarian aid organizations," the faxed letter said.
"I hope they are saying that I am in the residence because that would be the best proof that I am not involved since I can't be in two places at the same time."
